<details>
The PKGBUILD defines a standard source using a git repository with a signed tag reference (`git+https://github.com/archlinux/libudev0-shim.git#tag=v${pkgver}?signed`). Fetching this source involves a `git clone` of a known upstream repository tied to a specific signed tag, which is a trusted and common practice in AUR packages. The `pkgver` is hardcoded as `2`, so no dynamic version fetching occurs that could trigger arbitrary code execution. There is no command substitution, external network access, or execution of downloaded code during sourcing of the PKGBUILD. The `sha512sums` array is properly specified with a valid checksum, so integrity verification will occur during source download (though even if it were 'SKIP', that would not make this gate unsafe). No potentially dangerous operations are performed in the global scope or in `pkgver()`, as no such function is defined (and `pkgver=2` is static). Therefore, running `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` and `makepkg --printsrcinfo` is safe.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>
No malicious code execution during sourcing or source fetch
</summary>
